She couldn't breathe.

The doctor said bacteria from her dentures had gotten into her lungs while she slept. Aspiration pneumonia. He asked her when she'd last had them professionally cleaned.

She didn't know what to say.

I hung up the phone and stared at my own dentures sitting in a cup by the sink.

Clear plastic. Mint-scented water. Just like the instructions said.

And I knew—knew—I was next.

My name is Sarah. I'm 34 years old. And for the last three years, I've worn dentures.
